title: Atherosclerotic fibrous cap is synthesized by intimal smooth muscle cells
vignette: A 64-year-old man becomes unconscious after experiencing severe retrosternal chest pain. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia but is nonadherent with his prescribed medication regimen. He also has a long history of heavy smoking. Paramedics are called, and the man is pronounced dead on arrival to the emergency department. An autopsy reveals diffuse atherosclerotic vascular disease involving the coronary arteries. One of the atheromatous plaques in the left main artery has a ruptured fibrous cap with an overlying occluding thrombus. Which of the following cellular components is most directly involved in formation of the fibrous portion of this patient's plaque?

clues.text: diffuse atherosclerotic vascular disease involving the coronary arteries
clues.note: Chronic atherosclerosis (driven by hypertension, dyslipidemia, smoking) forms atheromatous plaques with a lipid core and a fibrous cap.

clues.text: ruptured fibrous cap with an overlying occluding thrombus
clues.note: Rupture of the FIBROUS CAP exposes thrombogenic material, causing acute coronary thrombosis; the question asks which cells build that fibrous cap.

whatMatters: The FIBROUS CAP of an atheroma is made by intimal SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS, which migrate from the media (stimulated by PDGF and other growth factors) and synthesize the EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX (COLLAGEN, proteoglycans) that forms the fibrous portion of the plaque. Answer E.
strategy: Separate the plaque's players: endothelial injury initiates it; foamy MACROPHAGES form the lipid core; T lymphocytes drive inflammation; platelets thrombose after rupture - but the FIBROUS CAP (collagen/ECM) is synthesized by SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS. Reject activated platelets (thrombosis after rupture), endothelial cells (injury/initiation, not cap synthesis), foamy macrophages (lipid core/foam cells), and T lymphocytes (inflammation).

eliminations.label: Activated platelets - thrombosis after rupture
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: platelets that aggregate and form thrombus when the cap ruptures. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they release growth factors (PDGF) and cause the acute occluding thrombus but do NOT synthesize the fibrous cap. ✅ Correct if: the overlying occluding thrombus.

eliminations.label: Endothelial cells - injury/initiation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the vessel lining whose dysfunction/injury initiates atherosclerosis (allows monocyte/LDL entry). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: endothelial injury starts the process but the cap's collagen is made by smooth muscle cells, not endothelium. ✅ Correct if: the initiating step (endothelial dysfunction).

eliminations.label: Foamy macrophages - lipid core, not cap
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: macrophages that engulf oxidized LDL to become foam cells. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they build the lipid/necrotic CORE and secrete cytokines/proteases (which weaken the cap), not the fibrous cap itself. ✅ Correct if: foam-cell/lipid-core formation.

eliminations.label: Infiltrating T lymphocytes - inflammation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: T cells that amplify plaque inflammation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they modulate the inflammatory response but do not synthesize the extracellular matrix of the fibrous cap. ✅ Correct if: the chronic inflammatory component.

reasoning: Atherosclerotic plaques have a lipid/necrotic core covered by a fibrous cap
The fibrous cap is composed of extracellular matrix (collagen, proteoglycans)
Intimal smooth muscle cells (migrating from the media under PDGF stimulation) synthesize this matrix
mechanism: ATHEROSCLEROSIS is a chronic inflammatory, fibroproliferative disease. It begins with ENDOTHELIAL CELL injury/dysfunction (from hypertension, hyperlipidemia, smoking, diabetes), which permits adhesion and migration of MONOCYTES and T LYMPHOCYTES into the intima and entry of LDL, which is oxidized and phagocytosed by macrophages to form lipid-laden FOAM CELLS (the fatty streak and lipid core). Activated leukocytes, dysfunctional endothelium, and adherent PLATELETS release cytokines and GROWTH FACTORS - notably PLATELET-DERIVED GROWTH FACTOR (PDGF), fibroblast growth factor, and endothelin-1 - that stimulate MEDIAL SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS to MIGRATE into the intima and PROLIFERATE. These intimal SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS synthesize EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX (COLLAGEN, elastin, proteoglycans), forming the FIBROUS CAP that overlies the lipid core (a mature atheroma/fibrofatty plaque). As the plaque enlarges - and as macrophage-derived proteases (metalloproteinases) degrade matrix - the cap can RUPTURE, exposing thrombogenic material and triggering acute luminal THROMBOSIS (acute coronary syndrome/sudden cardiac death). Thus the fibrous cap is made by smooth muscle cells; platelets, endothelium, foam cells, and T cells contribute to other aspects of the lesion.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Path/CV > atherosclerosis: endothelial injury -> monocyte/LDL entry -> foam cells (lipid core); PDGF/FGF stimulate medial smooth muscle cells to migrate/proliferate and synthesize collagen (fibrous cap); plaque rupture -> thrombosis (ACS).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Fibrous cap = collagen synthesized by intimal smooth muscle cells (PDGF-driven).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on fibrous cap, atheroma, foam cells, PDGF, smooth muscle migration, or plaque rupture? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Platelets = thrombosis; endothelium = initiation; foamy macrophages = lipid core; T cells = inflammation.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: fibrous cap of atheroma = smooth muscle cells producing collagen/ECM (PDGF); rupture -> thrombosis.

keywords.front: Cell building the atherosclerotic fibrous cap
Growth factor driving smooth muscle migration

firstAid.detail: Path: smooth muscle cells make collagen/ECM (PDGF).

memoryHook: Smooth muscle cells are the plaque's masons - they migrate in and lay down collagen to build the fibrous cap (PDGF is the whistle that calls them over).
